        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import contextlib
import datetime
import json
import logging
import operator
import pathlib
import shutil
import tempfile
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from .. import (
    bootstrap_requirement_resolver,
    build_environment,
    dependencies,
    gitutils,
    progress,
    sources,
)
from ..dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from ..log import req_ctxvar_context, requirement_ctxvar
from ..requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType
from . import _cache
from ._build import Build
from ._phase import Phase
from ._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from ._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from ._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from ._resolve import Resolve
from ._types import (
    _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    FailureRecord,
    FailureType,
    SeenKey,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from ._work_item import WorkItem

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .. import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Bootstrapper:
    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        progressbar: progress.Progressbar | None = None,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str | None = None,
        sdist_only: bool = False,
        test_mode: bool = False,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        num_bg_threads: int = _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    ) -> None:
        if test_mode and sdist_only:
            raise ValueError(
                "--test-mode requires full wheel builds; incompatible with --sdist-only"
            )

        self.ctx = ctx
        self.progressbar = progressbar or progress.Progressbar(None)
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url or ctx.wheel_server_url
        self.sdist_only = sdist_only
        self.test_mode = test_mode
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.why: list[tuple[RequirementType, Requirement, Version]] = []
        self._num_bg_threads = max(1, num_bg_threads)
        self._bg_pool: concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor | None = (
            concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix="fromager-bg"
            )
        )

        # Delegate resolution to BootstrapRequirementResolver
        self._resolver = bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver(
            ctx=ctx,
            prev_graph=prev_graph,
            multiple_versions=multiple_versions,
            cache_wheel_server_url=self.cache_wheel_server_url,
        )
        # Push items onto the stack as we start to resolve their
        # dependencies so at the end we have a list of items that need to
        # be built in order.
        self._build_stack: list[typing.Any] = []
        self._build_requirements: set[tuple[NormalizedName, str]] = set()

        # Track requirements we've seen before so we don't resolve the
        # same dependencies over and over and so we can break cycles in
        # the dependency list. The key is the requirements spec, rather
        # than the package, in case we do have multiple rules for the same
        # package.
        self._seen_requirements: set[SeenKey] = set()

        self._build_order_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "build-order.json"
        self._stack_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "bootstrap-stack.json"
        logger.info("recording bootstrap stack state to %s", self._stack_filename)

        # Track failed packages in test mode (list of typed dicts for JSON export)
        self.failed_packages: list[FailureRecord] = []

        # Track failed versions in multiple_versions mode
        self._failed_versions: dict[tuple[str, str], Exception] = {}

    @property
    def resolver(self) -> bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver:
        """Public accessor for the version resolver."""
        return self._resolver

    def has_failed_version(self, pkg_name: NormalizedName, version: Version) -> bool:
        """Return True if this (pkg_name, version) has previously failed resolution."""
        return (pkg_name, str(version)) in self._failed_versions

    def _resolve_and_add_top_level(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
    ) -> tuple[str, Version] | None:
        """Resolve a top-level requirement and add it to the dependency graph.

        Private method called only by ``bootstrap()``.

        This is the pre-resolution phase before recursive bootstrapping begins.
        In test mode, catches resolution errors and records them as failures.

        When multiple_versions is enabled, resolves and adds all matching versions
        to the graph, but still returns only the first (highest) version for
        backward compatibility.

        Args:
            req: The top-level requirement to resolve.

        Returns:
            Tuple of (source_url, version) if resolution succeeded, None if it
            failed in test mode.

        Raises:
            Exception: In normal mode, re-raises any resolution error.
        """
        try:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            results = self.resolve_versions(
                req=req,
                req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                parent_req=None,
                return_all_versions=self.multiple_versions,
            )
            if self.multiple_versions:
                logger.info(f"resolved {len(results)} version(s) for {req}")

            # Add all resolved versions to the graph
            for source_url, version in results:
                logger.info("%s resolves to %s", req, version)
                self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
                    parent_name=None,
                    parent_version=None,
                    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                    req=req,
                    req_version=version,
                    download_url=source_url,
                    pre_built=pbi.pre_built,
                    constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),
                )

            if not results:
                if self.multiple_versions:
                    err = RuntimeError(f"no versions found for {req}")
                    self._record_failed_version(
                        req, "unresolved", err, "no versions resolved, skipping"
                    )
                    if self.test_mode:
                        self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                    return None
                raise RuntimeError(f"Could not resolve any versions for {req}")

            # Return first result for backward compatibility
            return results[0]
        except Exception as err:
            if self.multiple_versions:
                self._record_failed_version(req, "unresolved", err, "failed to resolve")
                if self.test_mode:
                    self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                return None
            if not self.test_mode:
                raise
            self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
            return None

    def resolve_versions(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,

{"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "This is the fromager repository (Python wheel builder). A virtualenv with the project\nand test dependencies is already set up at `.venv`; run tests with\n`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts=\"\" tests/...`.\n\nFix the issue below. Add a regression test and run the relevant test file.\n\nIssue #1214: fromager might \"lie\" about the reason of a dependency resolution failure\n\nExpected: fromager states the exact reason of the broken dependency chain.\nActual: with ENABLE_REPEATABLE_BUILD_MODE and a broken indirect dependency, the error is\nlogged under whatever top-level package is active in the logging context, e.g.\n`ERROR its-hub: Unable to resolve requirement specifier flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 ...`\nwhile the real chain is its-hub -> reward-hub -> vllm and vllm is the broken arc.\nfromager should say the resolution is broken because of vllm, not its-hub."}, "timestamp": "2026-10-09T16:36:51.214Z"}

All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution\n        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types\n        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.\n        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)\n        # Value: {version: url}\n        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}\n        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.\n        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)\n        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.\n        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()\n        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def resolve(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,\n        pre_built: bool | None = None,\n        return_all_versions: bool = False,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).\n\n        Uses a two-step strategy:\n        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch\n           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the\n           package-level known-versions cache.\n        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current\n           requirement specifier.\n\n        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,\n        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups\n        with different specifiers for the same package.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            req_type: Type of requirement\n            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain\n            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).\n                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.\n            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,\n                return only the highest matching version.\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching\n            versions when return_all_versions=True.\n\n        Raises:\n            ValueError: If req contains a git URL and pre_built is False\n                (git URL source resolution must be handled by Bootstrapper)\n        \"\"\"\n        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key and URL guard)\n        if pre_built is None:\n            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n            pre_built = pbi.pre_built\n\n        # Check session cache BEFORE the git URL guard so that background\n        # threads can retrieve pre-cached git URL resolutions (populated by\n        # Bootstrapper.resolve_versions() on the main thread before bootstrap()\n        # is called) without hitting the ValueError.\n        cached_result = self.get_cached_resolution(req, pre_built)\n        if cached_result is not None:\n            logger.debug(f\"resolved {req} from cache\")\n            return list(cached_result) if return_all_versions else [cached_result[0]]\n\n        # Git URL source resolution must be handled by Bootstrapper.\n        # But git URL prebuilt resolution is allowed - we look for wheels on PyPI\n        # (test mode fallback uses this path).\n        if req.url and not pre_built:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Git URL requirements must be handled by Bootstrapper: {req}\"\n            )\n\n        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)\n\n        with self._lock:\n            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:\n                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and\n                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.\n                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)\n                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)\n            else:\n                logger.debug(f\"rule already resolved: {req}\")\n\n            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.\n            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n\n        if not matching:\n            return []\n        if return_all_versions:\n            return matching\n        return [matching[0]]\n\n    def get_cached_resolution(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        if not self.failed_packages:\n            logger.info(\"test mode: all packages processed successfully\")\n            return 0\n\n        # Write JSON failure report with timestamp for uniqueness\n        timestamp = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC).strftime(\"%Y%m%d-%H%M%S-%f\")\n        failures_file = self.ctx.work_dir / f\"test-mode-failures-{timestamp}.json\"\n        with open(failures_file, \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump({\"failures\": self.failed_packages}, f, indent=2)\n        logger.info(\"test mode: wrote failure report to %s\", failures_file)\n\n        # Exception,\n    ) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"Handle errors from phase processing.\n\n        Returns work items to continue processing (e.g. prebuilt fallback),\n        or empty list to skip this item. Raises in normal mode (fail-fast).\n        \"\"\"\n        wi = item.work_item\n        # Resolution failures: recoverable in test mode and multiple versions mode\n        if isinstance(item, Resolve):\n            if self.test_mode:\n                self.record_test_mode_failure(wi.req, None, err, \"resolution\")\n                if self.multiple_versions:\n                    self._record_failed_version(\n                        wi.req,\n                        \"unresolved\",\n                        err,\n                        f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n                    )\n                return []\n            if self.multiple_versions:\n                self._record_failed_version(\n                    wi.req,\n                    \"unresolved\",\n                    err,\n                    f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n                )\n                return []\n            raise\n\n        # Test mode: try prebuilt fallback for build-related phases\n        if self.test_mode:\n            if (\n                isinstance(item, PrepareSource | PrepareBuild | Build)\n                and not wi.pbi_pre_built\n            ):\n                assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n                fallback = self._handle_test_mode_failure(\n                    req=wi.req,\n                    resolved_version=wi.resolved_version,\n                    req_type=wi.req_type,\n                    build_error=err,\n                )\n                if fallback is not None:\n                    wi.build_result = fallback\n                    return [ProcessInstallDeps(wi)]\n            self.record_test_mode_failure(\n                wi.req, str(wi.resolved_version), err, \"bootstrap\"\n            )\n            return []\n\n        # Multiple versions mode: record failure, remove from graph, continue\n        if self.multiple_versions:\n            assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n            pkg_name = canonicalize_name(wi.req.name)\n            self._record_failed_version(\n                wi.req,\n                str(wi.resolved_version),\n                err,\n                f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n            )\n            self.ctx.dependency_graph.remove_dependency(pkg_name, wi.resolved_version)\n            self._seen_requirements.discard(\n                self._resolved_key(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, \"sdist\")\n            )\n            self._seen_requirements.discard(\n                self._resolved_key(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, \"wheel\")\n            )\n            self.ctx.write_to_graph_to_file()\n            return []\n\n        # Normal mode: fail-fast\n        raise\n\n    def _record_failed_version(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: str,\n        err: Exception,\n        detail: str,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Record a version failure in multiple versions mode.\"\"\"\n        pkg_name = canonicalize_name(req.name)\n        self._failed_versions[(pkg_name, version)] = err\n        logger.warning(\n            \"%s==%s: %s: %s: %s\",\n            req.name,\n            version,\n            detail,\n            type(err).__name__,\n            err,\n        )\n\n    def _log_failed_versions_table(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Log a summary table of all failed versions.\"\"\"\n        logger.warning(\"%d version(s) failed to bootstrap:\", len(self._failed_versions))\n        for (name, ver), exc in self._failed_versions.items():\n            logger.warning(\"  %s==%s: %s: %s\", name, ver, type(exc).__name__, exc)\n\n    def finalize(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Finalize bootstrap and return exit code.\n","numLines":110,"startLine":1125,"totalLines":1287}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_011w6h4CfYBuJf3Do1rc1qBh","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"rule"}}]}

Capture parent from current why stack before creating work items\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None = None\n        if self.why:\n            _, parent_req, parent_version = self.why[-1]\n            parent = (parent_req, parent_version)\n\n        # Save the why stack so we can restore it after the iterative loop\n        # (the loop modifies self.why for each work item)\n        saved_why = list(self.why)\n\n        # Single RESOLVE item — resolution, version expansion, and error\n        # handling all happen inside the loop via Resolve.run().\n        initial_item = Resolve(\n            WorkItem(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                why_snapshot=list(self.why),\n                parent=parent,\n            )\n        )\n        stack: list[Phase] = []\n        self._push_items(stack, [initial_item])\n\n        self._run_bootstrap_loop(stack)\n\n        # empty the stack state file to show watchers are are done\n        # with bootstrapping\n        self._record_stack_state([])\n\n        # Restore why stack for the caller\n        self.why = saved_why\n\n    @contextlib.contextmanager\n    def _track_why(\n        self,\n        item: Phase,\n    ) -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n        \"\"\"Context manager to track dependency chain in self.why stack.\n\n        No-op for phases where tracks_why is False (RESOLVE and START).\n        For all other phases, pushes the item onto the why stack and\n        ensures it is popped even if an exception occurs.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not item.tracks_why:\n            yield\n            return\n        wi = item.work_item\n        assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n        self.why.append((wi.req_type, wi.req, wi.resolved_version))\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            self.why.pop()\n\n    def record_test_mode_failure(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: str | None,\n        err: Exception,\n        failure_type: FailureType,\n        log_level: typing.Literal[\"error\", \"warning\"] = \"error\",\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Record a failure in test mode. version_str = f\"=={version}\" if version else \"\"\n        msg = f\"test mode: {failure_type} failed for {req.name}{version_str}\"\n        if log_level == \"warning\":\n            logger.warning(\"%s: %s (continuing)\", msg, err)\n        else:\n            logger.error(\"%s: %s\", msg, err, exc_info=True)\n\n        self.failed_packages.append(\n            {\n                \"package\": str(req.name),\n                \"version\": version,\n                \"exception_type\": err.__class__.__name__,\n                \"exception_message\": str(err),\n                \"failure_type\": failure_type,\n            }\n        )\n\n    @property\n    def explain(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Return message formatting current version of why stack.\"\"\"\n        return \" for \".join(\n            f\"{req_type} dependency {req} ({resolved_version})\"\n            for req_type, req, resolved_version in reversed(self.why)\n        )\n\n    def _prepare_build_dependencies(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version | None,\n        sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n        build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment,\n    ) -> set[Requirement]:\n        \"\"\"Prepare build dependencies for a package.\n\n        Only used by the git URL resolution path\n        (_resolve_version_from_git_url -> _get_version_from_package_metadata).\n        The main iterative bootstrap loop handles build deps via phase handlers.\n        \"\"\"\n        # build system\n        build_system_dependencies = dependencies.get_build_system_dependencies(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n        )\n        self._handle_build_requirements(\n            req,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM,\n            build_system_dependencies,\n        )\n        # The next hooks need build system requirements.\n        build_env.install(build_system_dependencies)\n\n        # build backend\n        build_backend_dependencies = dependencies.get_build_backend_dependencies(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n\n        # build sdist\n        build_sdist_dependencies = dependencies.get_build_sdist_dependencies(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n\n        # Filter out deps already satisfied by build-system dependencies\n        resolved_build_sys = self._resolve_build_system_versions_by_name(\n            build_system_dependencies,\n        )\n        build_backend_dependencies = self.filter_deps_satisfied_by_build_system(\n            build_backend_dependencies,\n            resolved_build_sys,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_BACKEND,\n        )\n        build_sdist_dependencies = self.filter_deps_satisfied_by_build_system(\n            build_sdist_dependencies,\n            resolved_build_sys,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_SDIST,\n        )\n\n        self._handle_build_requirements(\n            req,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_BACKEND,\n            build_backend_dependencies,\n        )\n        self._handle_build_requirements(\n            req,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_SDIST,\n            build_sdist_dependencies,\n        )\n\n        build_dependencies = build_sdist_dependencies | build_backend_dependencies\n        if build_dependencies.isdisjoint(build_system_dependencies):\n            build_env.install(build_dependencies)\n\n        return (\n            build_system_dependencies\n            | build_backend_dependencies\n            | build_sdist_dependencies\n        )\n\n    def _handle_build_requirements(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        build_type: RequirementType,\n        build_dependencies: set[Requirement],\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap build dependencies.\n\n        Only used by the git URL resolution path\n        (_resolve_version_from_git_url -> _get_version_from_package_metadata).\n        The main iterative bootstrap loop handles build deps via phase handlers.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.progressbar.update_total(len(build_dependencies))\n\n        for dep in self._sort_requirements(build_dependencies):\n            with req_ctxvar_context(dep):\n                # Save/restore self.why because the iterative bootstrap()\n                # modifies it internally for each work item.\n                saved_why = list(self.why)\n                self._bootstrap_one(req=dep, req_type=build_type)\n                self.why = saved_why\n            self.progressbar.update()\n\n    def _download_prebuilt(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        wheel_url: str,\n    ) -> tuple[pathlib.Path, pathlib.Path]:\n        result = _cache._bg_prepare_prebuilt(\n            self.ctx, req, req_type, resolved_version, wheel_url\n        )\n        assert result.wheel_filename is not None\n        assert result.unpack_dir is not None\n        return (result.wheel_filename, result.unpack_dir)\n\n    def _download_source(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        source_url: str,\n    ) -> pathlib.Path:\n        \"\"\"Download source for a package.\"\"\"\n        result: pathlib.Path = sources.download_source(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            download_url=source_url,\n        )\n        return result\n\n    def _prepare_source(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        source_filename: pathlib.Path,\n    ) -> pathlib.Path:\n        \"\"\"Prepare (unpack/patch) source for building.\"\"\"\n        result: pathlib.Path = sources.prepare_source(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            source_filename=source_filename,\n            version=resolved_version,\n        )\n        return result\n\n    def _handle_test_mode_failure(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        build_error: Exception,\n    ) -> SourceBuildResult | None:\n        \"\"\"Handle build failure in test mode by attempting pre-built fallback.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement that failed to build.\n            resolved_version: The version that was attempted.\n            req_type: The type of requirement (for fallback resolution).\n            build_error: The original exception from the build attempt.\n\n        Returns:\n            SourceBuildResult if fallback succeeded, None if fallback also failed.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.warning(\n            \"test mode: build failed for %s==%s, attempting pre-built fallback: %s\",\n            req.name,\n            resolved_version,\n            build_error,\n        )\n\n        try:\n            parent_req = self.why[-1][1] if self.why else None\n            results = self._resolver.resolve(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                parent_req=parent_req,\n                pre_built=True,  # Force prebuilt for test mode fallback\n            )\n            wheel_url, fallback_version = results[0]\n\n            if fallback_version != resolved_version:\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"test mode: version mismatch for %s - requested %s, fallback %s\",\n                    req.name,\n                    resolved_version,\n                    fallback_version,\n                )\n\n            wheel_filename, unpack_dir = self._download_prebuilt(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                resolved_version=fallback_version,\n                wheel_url=wheel_url,\n            )\n\n            logger.info(\n                \"test mode: successfully used pre-built wheel for %s==%s\",\n                req.name,\n                fallback_version,\n            )\n\n            # Package succeeded via fallback - no failure to record\n\n            return SourceBuildResult(\n                wheel_filename=wheel_filename,\n                sdist_filename=None,\n                unpack_dir=unpack_dir,\n                sdist_root_dir=None,\n                build_env=None,\n                source_type=SourceType.PREBUILT,\n            )\n\n        except Exception as fallback_error:\n            logger.error(\n                \"test mode: pre-built fallback also failed for %s: %s\",\n                req.name,\n                fallback_error,\n                exc_info=True,\n            )\n            # Return None to signal failure; bootstrap() will record via re-raised exception\n            return None\n\n    def _resolve_version_from_git_url(self, req: Requirement) -> tuple[str, Version]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve source path and version from a ``git+`` URL.\n\n        Parses the URL for an ``@ref`` version hint. If the ref is a valid\n        version, reuses an existing clone when possible. Otherwise, clones\n        the repo and extracts the version from package metadata.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        if not req.url:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to resolve from URL with no URL in {req}\")\n\n        # We start by not knowing where we would put the source because we don't\n        # know the version.\n        working_src_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None\n        version: Version | None = None\n\n        url_to_clone, git_ref = gitutils.parse_vcs_url(req.url, require_ref=False)\n        need_to_clone = False\n\n        if git_ref == gitutils.GIT_HEAD:\n            # No ref in URL, clone to discover the version.\n            logger.debug(\"no reference in URL, will clone\")\n            need_to_clone = True\n        else:\n            # If we have a reference, it might be a valid python version\n            # string, or not. It _must_ be a valid git reference. If it can\n            # be parsed as a valid python version, we assume the tag points\n            # to source that will think that is its version, so we allow\n            # reusing an existing cloned repo if there is one.\n            try:\n                version = Version(git_ref)\n            except ValueError:\n                logger.info(\n                    \"could not parse %r as a version, cloning to get the version\",\n                    git_ref,\n                )\n                need_to_clone = True\n            else:\n                logger.info(\"URL %s includes version %s\", req.url, version)\n                working_src_dir = (\n                    self.ctx.work_dir\n                    / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                    / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                )\n                if not working_src_dir.exists():\n                    need_to_clone = True\n                else:\n                    if self.ctx.cleanup:\n                        logger.debug(\"cleaning up %s to reclone\", working_src_dir)\n                        shutil.rmtree(working_src_dir)\n                        need_to_clone = True\n                    else:\n                        logger.info(\"reusing %s\", working_src_dir)\n\n        if need_to_clone:\n            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:\n                clone_dir = pathlib.Path(tmpdir) / \"src\"\n                sources.download_git_source(\n                    ctx=self.ctx,\n                    req=req,\n                    url_to_clone=url_to_clone,\n                    destination_dir=clone_dir,\n                    ref=git_ref,\n                )\n                if not version:\n                    # If we still do not have a version, get it from the package\n                    # metadata.\n                    version = self._get_version_from_package_metadata(req, clone_dir)\n                    logger.info(\"found version %s\", version)\n                    working_src_dir = (\n                        self.ctx.work_dir\n                        / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                        / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                    )\n                    if working_src_dir.exists():\n                        # We have to check if the destination directory exists\n                        # because if we were not given a version we did not\n                        # clean it up earlier. We do not use ctx.cleanup to\n                        # control this action because we cannot trust that the\n                        # destination directory is reusable because we have had\n                        # to compute the version and we cannot be sure that the\n                        # version is dynamic. Two different commits in the repo\n                        # could have the same version if that version is set\n                        # with static data in the repo instead of via a tag or\n                        # dynamically computed by something like setuptools-scm.\n                        logger.debug(\"cleaning up %s\", working_src_dir)\n                        shutil.rmtree(working_src_dir)\n                assert working_src_dir is not None\n                working_src_dir.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n                logger.info(\"moving cloned repo to %s\", working_src_dir)\n                shutil.move(clone_dir, str(working_src_dir))\n\n        if not version:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to determine version for {req}\")\n\n        if not working_src_dir:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to determine working source directory for {req}\")\n\n        logging.info(\"resolved from git URL to %s, %s\", working_src_dir, version)\n        return (str(working_src_dir), version)\n\n    def _get_version_from_package_metadata(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        source_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    ) -> Version:\n        pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n        build_dir = pbi.build_dir(source_dir)\n\n        logger.info(\n            \"preparing build dependencies so we can access the metadata to get the version\"\n        )\n        build_env = build_environment.BuildEnvironment(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            parent_dir=source_dir.parent,\n        )\n        build_dependencies = self._prepare_build_dependencies(\n            req=req,\n            resolved_version=None,\n            sdist_root_dir=source_dir,\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n        build_env.install(build_dependencies)\n\n        logger.info(\"generating metadata to get version\")\n        hook_caller = dependencies.get_build_backend_hook_caller(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            build_dir=build_dir,\n            override_environ={},\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n        metadata_dir_base = hook_caller.prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel(\n            metadata_directory=str(source_dir.parent),\n            config_settings=pbi.config_settings,\n        )\n        metadata_filename = source_dir.parent / metadata_dir_base / \"METADATA\"\n        # Disable validation because some packages have metadata version mismatches\n        # (e.g., declaring Metadata-Version: 2.2 but using fields from 2.4).\n        metadata = dependencies.parse_metadata(metadata_filename, validate=False)\n        return metadata.version\n\n    def add_to_graph(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        req_version: Version,\n        download_url: str,\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a resolved requirement as a node/edge in the dependency graph.\n\n        Records the dependency relationship between ``parent`` and ``req`` in\n        the in-memory graph, then writes the updated graph to disk. Must be\n        called after resolution but before the seen-check so that every edge\n        is captured even for packages that are not built again.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement being added.\n            req_type: Whether this is a build-system, build-backend, install,\n                or other dependency kind.\n            req_version: The resolved version of ``req``.\n            download_url: Source URL used to obtain the distribution.\n            parent: ``(req, version)`` of the package that introduced ``req``,\n                or ``None`` for top-level requirements.\n        \"\"\"\n        parent_req, parent_version = parent if parent else (None, None)\n        pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n        # Update the dependency graph after we determine that this requirement is\n        # useful but before we determine if it is redundant so that we capture all\n        # edges to use for building a valid constraints file.\n        self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(\n            parent_name=canonicalize_name(parent_req.name) if parent_req else None,\n            parent_version=parent_version,\n            req_type=req_type,\n            req=req,\n            req_version=req_version,\n            download_url=download_url,\n            pre_built=pbi.pre_built,\n            constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),\n        )\n        self.ctx.write_to_graph_to_file()\n\n    def _sort_requirements(\n        self,\n        requirements: typing.Iterable[Requirement],\n    ) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:\n        return sorted(requirements, key=operator.attrgetter(\"name\"))\n\n    def _resolved_key(\n        self, req: Requirement, version: Version, typ: typing.Literal[\"sdist\", \"wheel\"]\n    ) -> SeenKey:\n        return (\n            canonicalize_name(req.name),\n            tuple(sorted(req.extras)),\n            str(version),\n            typ,\n        )\n\n    def mark_as_seen(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        sdist_only: bool = False,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Track sdist and wheel builds\n\n        A sdist-only build just contains as an sdist.\n        A wheel build counts as wheel and sdist, because the presence of a\n        either implies we have built a wheel from an sdist or we have a\n        prebuilt wheel that will never have an sdist.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Mark sdist seen for sdist-only build and wheel build\n        self._seen_requirements.add(self._resolved_key(req, version, \"sdist\"))\n        if not sdist_only:\n            # Mark wheel seen only for wheel build\n            self._seen_requirements.add(self._resolved_key(req, version, \"wheel\"))\n\n    def has_been_seen(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        sdist_only: bool = False,\n    ) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True if this requirement/version has already been processed.\n\n        Uses the same sdist-vs-wheel distinction as ``mark_as_seen``:\n        when ``sdist_only`` is True, checks only for a prior sdist build;\n        otherwise checks for a prior wheel build.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement to check.\n            version: The resolved version to check.\n            sdist_only: If True, check for a sdist-only build instead of a\n                full wheel build.\n        \"\"\"\n        typ: typing.Literal[\"sdist\", \"wheel\"] = \"sdist\" if sdist_only else \"wheel\"\n        return self._resolved_key(req, version, typ) in self._seen_requirements\n\n    def add_to_build_order(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        source_url: str,\n        source_type: SourceType,\n        prebuilt: bool = False,\n        constraint: Requirement | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a package to the build-order output file if not already present.\n\n        Deduplicates by ``(canonicalized_name, version)`` so the same package\n        is never written twice, regardless of extras. On each new entry, the\n        full build-order list is written to ``self._build_order_filename``.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement being added to the build order.\n            version: The resolved version.\n            source_url: URL from which the source distribution was obtained.\n            source_type: The kind of source (sdist, wheel, git, etc.).\n            prebuilt: True if the wheel was taken from a prebuilt cache rather\n                than compiled locally.\n            constraint: The version constraint active for this package, if any.\n        \"\"\"\n        # We only care if this version of this package has been built,\n        # and don't want to trigger building it twice. The \"extras\"\n        # value, included in the _resolved_key() output, can confuse\n        # that so we ignore itand build our own key using just the\n        # name and version.\n        key = (canonicalize_name(req.name), str(version))\n        if key in self._build_requirements:\n            return\n        logger.info(f\"adding {key} to build order\")\n        self._build_requirements.add(key)\n        info = {\n            \"req\": str(req),\n            \"constraint\": str(constraint) if constraint else \"\",\n            \"dist\": canonicalize_name(req.name),\n            \"version\": str(version),\n            \"prebuilt\": prebuilt,\n            \"source_url\": source_url,\n            \"source_url_type\": str(source_type),\n        }\n        if req.url:\n            info[\"source_url\"] = req.url\n        self._build_stack.append(info)\n        with open(self._build_order_filename, \"w\") as f:\n            # Set default=str because the why value includes\n            # Requirement and Version instances that can't be\n            # converted to JSON without help.\n            json.dump(self._build_stack, f, indent=2, default=str)\n\n    def _record_stack_state(self, stack: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Write the current bootstrap stack to `self._stack_filename`.\n\n        Index 0 in the output corresponds to `stack[-1]`, the next item to be\n        processed. Overwrites the file on each call.\n        \"\"\"\n        records = [item.as_json() for item in reversed(stack)]\n        with open(self._stack_filename, \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump(records, f, indent=2, default=str)\n\n    # ---- Iterative bootstrap: phase handlers and helpers ----\n\n    def _push_items(self, stack: list[Phase], items: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Push items onto the stack and submit background tasks in LIFO order.\n\n        Submits the item that will be processed first (top of stack) to the\n        background pool first, maximising overlap between background I/O and\n        main-thread serial work.\n        \"\"\"\n        stack.extend(items)\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            for item in reversed(items):\n                bg_work = item.background_work(self)\n                if bg_work is not None:\n                    item.bg_future = self._bg_pool.submit(bg_work)\n\n    def _drain_background_pool(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drain all in-flight background tasks and recreate the pool.\n\n        Used as an exclusive-build barrier: ensures all background I/O completes\n        before an exclusive build starts. ``cancel_futures=False`` guarantees\n        every submitted task runs to completion.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            self._bg_pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=False)\n            self._bg_pool = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(\n                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix=\"fromager-bg\"\n            )\n\n    def create_unresolved_work_items(\n        self,\n        deps: typing.Iterable[Requirement],\n        dep_req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement,\n        parent_version: Version,\n    ) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"Create RESOLVE-phase work items for dependencies.\n\n        Called inside a parent's _track_why context so that why_snapshot\n        captures the parent's dependency chain. Resolution and error\n        handling happen later when each item's RESOLVE phase runs.\n        \"\"\"\n        return [\n            Resolve(\n                WorkItem(\n                    req=dep,\n                    req_type=dep_req_type,\n                    why_snapshot=list(self.why),\n                    parent=(parent_req, parent_version),\n                )\n            )\n            for dep in self._sort_requirements(deps)\n        ]\n\n    def _resolve_build_system_versions_by_name(\n        self,\n        build_system_deps: set[Requirement],\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system versions by looking up graph nodes.\n\n        Used by the git URL path where the parent node may not yet exist\n        in the dependency graph.\n        \"\"\"\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for dep in build_system_deps:\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            nodes = self.ctx.dependency_graph.get_nodes_by_name(str(dep_name))\n            for node in nodes:\n                if node.version in dep.specifier:\n                    resolved[dep_name] = (node.version, node.download_url)\n                    break\n        return resolved\n\n    def get_resolved_build_system_versions(\n        self,\n        item: WorkItem,\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system dependency versions.\n\n        Looks up the parent node's ``BUILD_SYSTEM`` edges in the dependency\n        graph to find what versions were resolved for each build-system\n        dependency.\n\n        Returns:\n            Mapping of canonicalized package name to ``(version, download_url)``.\n        \"\"\"\n        assert item.resolved_version is not None\n        parent_key = f\"{canonicalize_name(item.req.name)}=={item.resolved_version}\"\n        parent_node = self.ctx.dependency_graph.nodes.get(parent_key)\n        if parent_node is None:\n            return {}\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for edge in parent_node.children:\n            if edge.req_type == RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM:\n                child = edge.destination_node\n                resolved[child.canonicalized_name] = (\n                    child.version,\n                    child.download_url,\n                )\n        return resolved\n\n    def filter_deps_satisfied_by_build_system(\n        self,\n        deps: set[Requirement],\n        resolved_build_sys: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]],\n        dep_req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None = None,\n    ) -> set[Requirement]:\n        \"\"\"Filter out deps already satisfied by build-system dependencies.\n\n        For each dep whose resolved build-system version satisfies the\n        requirement specifier, excludes the dep from the returned set.\n        When *parent* is provided, also adds a graph edge reusing that\n        version.  Remaining deps need independent resolution.\n\n        Logs a warning when the same package appears in both build-system\n        and build-backend/sdist with incompatible version specifiers.\n        \"\"\"\n        unsatisfied: set[Requirement] = set()\n        for dep in deps:\n            if dep.extras:\n                unsatisfied.add(dep)\n                continue\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            if dep_name in resolved_build_sys:\n                version, download_url = resolved_build_sys[dep_name]\n                if version in dep.specifier:\n                    logger.info(\n                        \"%s dependency %s is already satisfied by \"\n                        \"build-system dependency %s==%s\",\n                        dep_req_type,\n                        dep,\n                        dep_name,\n                        version,\n                    )\n                    if parent is not None:\n                        self.add_to_graph(\n                            req=dep,\n                            req_type=dep_req_type,\n                            req_version=version,\n                            download_url=download_url,\n                            parent=parent,\n                        )\n                    continue\n                else:\n                    logger.warning(\n                        \"%s dependency %s conflicts with \"\n                        \"build-system dependency %s==%s; \"\n                        \"resolving independently\",\n                        dep_req_type,\n                        dep,\n                        dep_name,\n                        version,\n                    )\n            unsatisfied.add(dep)\n        return unsatisfied\n\n    def _handle_phase_error(\n        self,\n        item: Phase,\n        err: Exception,\n    ) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"Handle errors from phase processing.\n\n        Returns work items to continue processing (e.g. prebuilt fallback),\n        or empty list to skip this item. Raises in normal mode (fail-fast).\n        \"\"\"\n        wi = item.work_item\n        # Resolution failures: recoverable in test mode and multiple versions mode\n        if isinstance(item, Resolve):\n            if self.test_mode:\n                self.record_test_mode_failure(wi.req, None, err, \"resolution\")\n                if self.multiple_versions:\n                    self._record_failed_version(\n                        wi.req,\n                        \"unresolved\",\n                        err,\n                        f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n                    )\n                return []\n            if self.multiple_versions:\n                self._record_failed_version(\n                    wi.req,\n                    \"unresolved\",\n                    err,\n                    f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n                )\n                return []\n            raise\n\n        # Test mode: try prebuilt fallback for build-related phases\n        if self.test_mode:\n            if (\n                isinstance(item, PrepareSource | PrepareBuild | Build)\n                and not wi.pbi_pre_built\n            ):\n                assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n                fallback = self._handle_test_mode_failure(\n                    req=wi.req,\n                    resolved_version=wi.resolved_version,\n                    req_type=wi.req_type,\n                    build_error=err,\n                )\n                if fallback is not None:\n                    wi.build_result = fallback\n                    return [ProcessInstallDeps(wi)]\n            self.record_test_mode_failure(\n                wi.req, str(wi.resolved_version), err, \"bootstrap\"\n            )\n            return []\n\n        # """Tests for --test-mode feature.

Tests the test mode functionality:
- Bootstrapper initialization with test_mode flag
- Exception handling: catch errors, log, continue
- Bootstrapper.finalize() exit codes
- JSON failure report generation
- failure_type field for categorizing failures
"""

import json
import logging
import pathlib
from unittest import mock

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import bootstrapper, context
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType


class TestBootstrapperInitialization:
    """Test Bootstrapper initialization with test_mode parameter."""

    def test_test_mode_enabled(self, tmp_context: context.WorkContext) -> None:
        """Test Bootstrapper with test_mode=True."""
        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context, test_mode=True)
        assert bt.test_mode is True
        assert isinstance(bt.failed_packages, list)
        assert len(bt.failed_packages) == 0

    def test_test_mode_disabled_by_default(
        self, tmp_context: context.WorkContext
    ) -> None:
        """Test Bootstrapper with test_mode=False (default)."""
        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context)
        assert bt.test_mode is False

    def test_test_mode_incompatible_with_sdist_only(
        self, tmp_context: context.WorkContext
    ) -> None:
        """Test that test_mode and sdist_only are mutually exclusive."""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="--test-mode requires full wheel builds"):
            bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context, test_mode=True, sdist_only=True)


class TestFinalizeExitCodes:
    """Test finalize() returns correct exit codes."""

    def test_finalize_no_failures_returns_zero(
        self, tmp_context: context.WorkContext
    ) -> None:
        """Test finalize returns 0 when no failures in test mode."""
        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context, test_mode=True)
        assert bt.finalize() == 0

    def test_finalize_with_failures_returns_one(
        self, tmp_context: context.WorkContext
    ) -> None:
        """Test finalize returns 1 when there are failures in test mode."""
        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context, test_mode=True)
        bt.failed_packages.append(
            {
                "package": "failing-pkg",
                "version": "1.0.0",
                "exception_type": "RuntimeError",
                "exception_message": "Build failed",
                "failure_type": "bootstrap",
            }
        )
        assert bt.finalize() == 1

    def test_finalize_not_in_test_mode_returns_zero(
        self, tmp_context: context.WorkContext
    ) -> None:
        """Test finalize returns 0 when not in test mode (regardless of failures)."""
        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context, test_mode=False)
        # Even if we manually add failures (shouldn't happen), it returns 0
        bt.failed_packages.append(
            {
                "package": "some-pkg",
                "version": "1.0.0",
                "exception_type": "RuntimeError",
                "exception_message": "Error",
                "failure_type": "bootstrap",
            }
        )
        assert bt.finalize() == 0

    def test_finalize_logs_failed_packages(
        self, tmp_context: context.WorkContext, caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture
    ) -> None:
        """Test finalize logs the list of failed packages."""
        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context, test_mode=True)
        bt.failed_packages.extend(

def _find_failure_report(work_dir: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path | None:
    """Find the test-mode-failures-*.json file in work_dir."""
    reports = list(work_dir.glob("test-mode-failures-*.json"))
    return reports[0] if reports else None


class TestJsonFailureReport:
    """Test JSON failure report generation."""

    def test_finalize_writes_json_report(
        self, tmp_context: context.WorkContext
    ) -> None:
        """Test finalize writes test-mode-failures-<timestamp>.json with failure details."""
        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context, test_mode=True)
        bt.failed_packages.append(
            {
                "package": "failing-pkg",
                "version": "1.0.0",
                "exception_type": "CalledProcessError",
                "exception_message": "Compilation failed",
                "failure_type": "bootstrap",
            }
        )

        bt.finalize()

        report_path = _find_failure_report(tmp_context.work_dir)
        assert report_path is not None
        assert report_path.name.startswith("test-mode-failures-")
        assert report_path.name.endswith(".json")

        with open(report_path) as f:
            report = json.load(f)

        assert "failures" in report
        assert len(report["failures"]) == 1
        assert report["failures"][0]["package"] == "failing-pkg"
        assert report["failures"][0]["version"] == "1.0.0"
        assert report["failures"][0]["exception_type"] == "CalledProcessError"
        assert report["failures"][0]["exception_message"] == "Compilation failed"
        assert report["failures"][0]["failure_type"] == "bootstrap"

    def test_finalize_no_report_when_no_failures(

    ) -> None:
        """Test finalize does not write report when there are no failures."""
        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(ctx=tmp_context, test_mode=True)

        bt.finalize()

        report_path = _find_failure_report(tmp_context.work_dir)
        assert report_path is None

"""Requirement resolution for bootstrap process.

Handles PyPI and graph-based resolution strategies.
Git URL resolution stays in Bootstrapper (orchestration concern).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from . import finders, resolver, sources, wheels
from .dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from .requirements_file import RequirementType

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class BootstrapRequirementResolver:
    """Resolve package requirements from PyPI or dependency graph during bootstrap.

    Single Responsibility: Coordinate resolution strategies for bootstrap process.
    Reason to Change: Resolution algorithm or provider priorities change.

    Resolution strategies (in order):
    1. Previous dependency graph (if available)
    2. PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)

    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper
    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize requirement resolver.

        Args:
            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings
            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching
            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through
                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the
                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other
                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.
            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.
                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.
        """
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url
        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution
        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types
        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.
        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)
        # Value: {version: url}
        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}
        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.
        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)
        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.
        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()
        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def resolve(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,
        pre_built: bool | None = None,
        return_all_versions: bool = False,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:
        """Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).

        Uses a two-step strategy:
        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch
           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the
           package-level known-versions cache.
        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current
           requirement specifier.

        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,
        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups
        with different specifiers for the same package.

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            req_type: Type of requirement
            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain
            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).
                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.
            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,
                return only the highest matching version.

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).
            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching
            versions when return_all_versions=True.

        """
        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key)
        if pre_built is None:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            pre_built = pbi.pre_built

        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)

        with self._lock:
            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:
                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and
                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.
                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)
                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)
            else:
                logger.debug(f"rule already resolved: {req}")

            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.
            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)

        if not matching:
            return []
        if return_all_versions:
            return matching
        return [matching[0]]

    def get_cached_resolution(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        pre_built: bool,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:
        """Return cached matching versions if this requirement was already resolved.

        Returns ``None`` if the requirement has not been resolved yet, allowing
        callers to distinguish between "no matching versions" and "not yet resolved".

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples if previously resolved, None otherwise.
        """
        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)
        with self._lock:
            if rule_key in self._resolved_rules:
                return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)
        return None

    def _resolve_and_extend(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        pre_built: bool,
        parent_req: Requirement | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Resolve versions from graph/network and extend known versions cache."""
        # Try previous dependency graph
        cached_resolution = self._resolve_from_graph(
            req=req,
            req_type=req_type,
            pre_built=pre_built,
            parent_req=parent_req,
        )

        if cached_resolution:
            logger.debug(
                f"resolved from previous bootstrap: {len(cached_resolution)} version(s)"
            )
            results = cached_resolution
        elif pre_built:
            # Resolve prebuilt wheel
            wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(
                self.ctx, req, cache_wheel_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL
            )
            results = wheels.resolve_all_prebuilt_wheels(
                ctx=self.ctx,
                req=req,
                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,
                req_type=req_type,
            )
        else:
            # Resolve source (sdist)
            provider = sources.get_source_provider(
                ctx=self.ctx,
                req=req,
                sdist_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL,
                req_type=req_type,
            )

# Based on https://github.com/sarugaku/resolvelib/blob/main/examples/pypi_wheel_provider.py
#
# Modified to look at sdists instead of wheels and to avoid trying to
# resolve any dependencies.
#
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import enum
import functools
import logging
import os
import re
import typing
from collections.abc import Iterable
from operator import attrgetter
from platform import python_version
from urllib.parse import quote, urlparse

import pypi_simple
import resolvelib
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.specifiers import InvalidSpecifier, SpecifierSet
from packaging.tags import Tag, sys_tags
from packaging.utils import (
    BuildTag,
    canonicalize_name,
    parse_wheel_filename,
)
from packaging.version import Version
from requests.models import Response
from resolvelib.resolvers import RequirementInformation

from . import overrides
from .candidate import Candidate, Cooldown
from .constraints import Constraints
from .downloads import extract_filename_from_url as extract_filename_from_url
from .extras_provider import ExtrasProvider
from .http_retry import RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS, retry_on_exception
from .request_session import session
from .requirements_file import RequirementType
from .versionmap import VersionMap

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PYTHON_VERSION = Version(python_version())
DEBUG_RESOLVER = os.environ.get("DEBUG_RESOLVER", "")
PYPI_SERVER_URL = "https://pypi.org/simple"
GITHUB_URL = "https://github.com"

# all supported tags
SUPPORTED_TAGS: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(sys_tags())
# same, but ignore the platform for 'ignore_platform' flag
IGNORE_PLATFORM: str = "ignore"
SUPPORTED_TAGS_IGNORE_PLATFORM: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(
    Tag(t.interpreter, t.abi, IGNORE_PLATFORM) for t in SUPPORTED_TAGS
)


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )


def _compute_max_age_cutoff(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
) -> datetime.datetime | None:
    """Compute the cutoff time for max release age filtering.

    Returns the oldest acceptable upload time, or None if disabled.
    Uses the cooldown's bootstrap_time for consistency across a single run.
    """
    if ctx.max_release_age is None:
        return None

{"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "This is the fromager repository (Python wheel builder). A virtualenv with the project\nand test dependencies is already set up at `.venv`; run tests with\n`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts=\"\" tests/...`.\n\nImplement the following change to the resolver's max-release-age handling\n(`src/fromager/resolver.py`, `find_all_matching_from_provider()`, and its callers in\n`src/fromager/bootstrap_requirement_resolver.py`).\n\n1. Replace the boolean `fallback_on_empty_age_filter` parameter of\n   `find_all_matching_from_provider()` with an `AgeFallback` enum (exported from\n   `fromager.resolver`) selecting what happens when age filtering removes every candidate:\n   - `AgeFallback.ALL`: keep every candidate (this is the single-version default and the\n     current behaviour, including its \"keeping all to avoid empty resolution\" warning)\n   - `AgeFallback.NEWEST`: keep only the single newest candidate (new)\n   - `AgeFallback.NONE`: return an empty list\n   Name the new keyword parameter `age_fallback`, default `AgeFallback.ALL`.\n   Log on the `fromager.resolver` logger when the fallback triggers, with these exact\n   messages (`%s`/`%d` formatting, `name` is `req.name`):\n   - ALL, warning: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days, keeping all to avoid empty resolution\"`\n   - NEWEST, info: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days, falling back to newest version %s\"`\n   - NONE, info: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days\"`\n   Multi-version bootstrap mode must use `AgeFallback.NEWEST`, so that when a dependency\n   has no release inside the age window (bar from two years ago depended on by a recent\n   foo) its newest version is built instead of failing, which avoids cascading failures\n   in the dependent package.\n\n2. Packages whose constraint pins an exact version (the provider's `constraints` object\n   returns a constraint for the requirement name and that constraint is a single `==`\n   specifier) skip age filtering entirely. A pin is explicit user intent and must not be\n   overridden by the age heuristic. Range constraints (`>=`, `<`, `!=`, ...) are still\n   age-filtered like unconstrained packages. Log at INFO on the\n   `fromager.resolver` logger: `\"%s: skipping age filter for pinned constraint (%d candidate(s))\"`.\n   Previously, in multi-version mode a constrained package pinned to a version older than\n   the window lost every candidate and resolution failed silently; in single-version mode\n   the fallback kept all candidates but logged the misleading warning.\n\nUpdate docstrings, add tests in `tests/test_cooldown.py` and\n`tests/test_bootstrap_requirement_resolver.py`, and run both files."}, "timestamp": "2026-10-09T16:37:50.737Z"}

"""Tests for bootstrap_requirement_resolver module."""

from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import resolver
from fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver import BootstrapRequirementResolver
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

# Test fixture: previous dependency graph
old_graph = DependencyGraph()

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("foo"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("foo"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
    req_version=Version("7"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("bar"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("bar"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
    req_version=Version("6"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("blah"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("blah"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
    req_version=Version("5"),
)


def test_resolve_from_graph_no_changes(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves from previous graph with no changes."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Resolving new dependency that doesn't exist in graph
    assert (
        resolver._resolve_from_graph(
            req=Requirement("xyz"),
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            pre_built=False,
            parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
        )
        is None
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("7"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_upgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver prefers top-level requirements over history."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr==8
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr==8"),
        req_version=Version("8"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - should get upgraded version from top-level
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("8"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - constraint prevents upgrade
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_downgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver handles version downgrades from top-level requirements."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr<=6"),
        req_version=Version("6"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - gets downgraded to 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - already at 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]
